title: Creational patterns: Singleton, Factory, Builder, Prototype
description: How objects get created: when to reach for a factory, a builder or a prototype, and why Singleton is the one to handle with care.

questions.text: What is the main job of a creational pattern?

options.text: To store objects in a database
To separate how objects are created and configured from the code that uses them

questions.explanation: Creational patterns hide construction details (which class, which arguments, how many instances) behind a stable interface, so callers do not depend on concrete types.

questions.text: A `Notification` can be email, SMS or push, chosen at runtime from a setting. Which pattern lets the caller ask for "a notification" without naming the class?
questions.explanation: A factory takes the choice (a type key or config) and returns the right implementation behind a common interface. The caller never writes `new SmsNotification()`.

questions.text: What does Abstract Factory add beyond a single Factory Method?

options.text: It builds one product at a time
It creates whole families of related objects that must match (for example a dark-theme button, checkbox and dialog)

questions.explanation: Abstract Factory groups several factory methods so a consistent set of products comes from one place. Mixing a Windows button with a Mac checkbox becomes impossible by construction.

questions.text: A `Report` has 12 optional settings, and the constructor call is unreadable. Which pattern fits best?
questions.explanation: Builder assembles an object step by step with named methods, validates it at `build()`, and avoids telescoping constructors with many positional arguments.

questions.text: Which problem is Prototype designed for?

options.text: Limiting a class to one instance
Creating a new object by copying an existing configured one, instead of building it from scratch

questions.explanation: Prototype clones a ready-made instance, useful when construction is expensive or the object is configured at runtime. The catch is deep versus shallow copies of nested state.

questions.text: A Singleton is simply a global variable with a nicer name, and it makes code harder to test.
questions.explanation: Mostly true. A Singleton gives hidden global state and ties callers to a concrete class, which hurts tests. Create one instance at the composition root and inject it instead, where one instance is truly needed.

questions.text: Which are real problems with a classic Singleton?

options.text: Tests share state and can affect each other
Dependencies are hidden inside methods instead of the constructor

questions.explanation: Shared state, hidden dependencies and race conditions in lazy initialisation are the usual costs. A Singleton can hold data; that is exactly what makes it risky.

questions.text: A pool of 20 database connections is reused instead of opened per request. Which pattern is this?
questions.explanation: Object Pool keeps expensive-to-create objects ready for reuse. It must make sure an object is reset when returned and that exhaustion is handled.

questions.text: Why might a Builder's `build()` method validate the data?

options.text: So that an invalid object can never be created

questions.explanation: Collecting fields first and checking the combination at the end means the finished object is always consistent, instead of half-initialised.

questions.text: Which statement about Simple Factory versus Factory Method is correct?

options.text: Simple Factory is one function or class with a conditional; Factory Method lets subclasses decide which product to create
Simple Factory requires an interface per product
They are identical in the GoF book

questions.explanation: Simple Factory is a common idiom (not a GoF pattern) that centralises `new`. Factory Method defers the choice to subclasses through an overridable creation method.

questions.text: You see `if (type == "pdf") new PdfExporter() else if (type == "csv") ...` repeated in five places. What is the best first refactor?

options.text: Copy it to a sixth place
Pull it into one factory or registry and call that everywhere

questions.explanation: Centralising the choice means a new type is added in one place. A registry keyed by type also keeps the factory closed for modification.
